results.question: What is scaled dot-product attention?
results.answer: Scaled Dot-Product Attention is an attention mechanism where the input consists of queries and keys of dimension d_k, and values of dimension d_v [S1]. It computes the dot products of the query with all keys, divides each by the square root of d_k (√d_k), and then applies a softmax function to derive the weights for the values [S1]. This process can be performed simultaneously on sets of queries, keys, and values packed into matrices Q, K, and V, with the output matrix computed as Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / √d_k)V [S1]. The scaling factor of 1/√d_k is used to counteract the effect of large dot product magnitudes for larger values of d_k, which can push the softmax function into regions with extremely small gradients [S1, S2]. Without this scaling factor, it is identical to dot-product (multiplicative) attention [S1, S2].

results.question: What BLUE score did the model achieve on Englsih to German translation?
results.answer: The Transformer (big) model achieved a BLEU score of 28.4 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, establishing a new state-of-the-art [S1, S4]. The Transformer base model achieved a BLEU score of 27.3 on the same task [S2].

results.question: How does the Transformer reduce training time compared with recurrent models?
results.answer: Recurrent models are inherently sequential, which prevents parallelization within training examples [S1]. In contrast, the Transformer model eschews recurrence and relies entirely on an attention mechanism, which allows for significantly more parallelization [S2]. This increased parallelization enables the Transformer to train in significantly less time compared to recurrent models [S2, S3]. For instance, it can achieve state-of-the-art translation quality after training for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs [S2], or establish a new state-of-the-art BLEU score for English-to-French translation after 3.5 days on eight GPUs, which is a small fraction of the training costs of other top models [S3].

results.question: How many parallel attention heads are used in the Transformer?
results.answer: The Transformer model uses 8 parallel attention layers, also referred to as heads [S1, S3].
